configs.description: The TM-280, fed from its external 5 VDC adaptor. The 2021 edition's footnote says "'z' specifies power supply and cord types": NA, EUR and UK (an AC adaptor with that cord), DC (a DC-DC adaptor) and AC (an adaptor with no cord). The adaptor is outside the box, so every z build has this face; the base is drawn without asserting which adaptor feeds it.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: telco.com publishes data sheets only; hardware documentation is on a support portal behind a login, whose contact is on telco.com/support. Searched: the telco.com media library, every product and knowledge-centre page, and the Wayback index of telco.com PDFs.

gaps.note: The left third of the face (wordmark plate, model name, CON, STS/PWR, pinhole, laser label) is drawn from the stencil master alone; the three-quarter renders cannot be rectified there with confidence, and the stencil was shown wrong elsewhere on this face by 2-2.5 mm.

chassis.note: 221 x 44 x 140.5 - the data sheet's "44 mm x 221 mm x 140.5 mm (1.73 in x 8.7 in x 5.51 in)"; the stencil master's outline is 221.6 x 44.4. The face has rounded end-caps, which the rectangular panel does not draw. BOTH EDITIONS PRINT "0.6 kg (2.42 lbs)", which disagree with themselves (2.42 lb is 1.10 kg, the TM-340's figure); 0.6 kg is carried as the metric figure both print, and the conflict is recorded here.

far-right-slot.note: A white oval slot or lug near the right end-cap (the render has it at about 207.5-216 x 30-33.5, beyond the fitted span; the stencil draws a small rectangle at 207.2-213.8, 32.9-34.6) is drawn as panel decor between the two. Nothing held says what it is - a light pipe or a lock slot are both plausible.

front-layout.note: TWO SOURCES, EACH WHERE IT HOLDS. The only renders are three-quarter views, and the face's rounded end-caps give no clean corners to rectify on, so a homography was fitted instead on the corners of the 1/1 and 3/1 legend boxes, taken from the stencil master TMC-280-x (CF). Inside that span the stencil and the rectified render agree to about 0.5 mm in x (the 1/1 lamp, both SFP cages and the 3/1 jack), so the frame is sound there; outside it the fit extrapolates badly - the CON bezel comes out half as big again as the Access jacks - so it is not used. POSITIONS IN THE PORT AREA (x 75-205) ARE THE RENDER'S: the Access pair is a ganged 2-jack block on a 14.05 pitch (the stencil draws two separate housings 16.5 apart), the RJ45s sit about 2 mm higher than the stencil has them, and the DC jack 1.7 mm left and 3 mm higher; the port numerals, the Network bracket's drops and its word sit where the render prints them, measured by clustering the glyphs in the rectified image: 1/1 at 97.45, 2/1 at 122.3 and 2/2 at 137.1 are within half a millimetre of their jacks and are drawn centred on them, and 3/1 at 166.95 is centred on its legend box rather than on its cage-and-jack pair (168.57), so it is drawn where it is printed and L61 stays in the baseline for it on purpose. The Network word is at 133.5. THE LEFT GROUP - the wordmark plate, T-Marc 280, CON, STS, PWR, the pinhole and the laser label - IS THE STENCIL'S, unchecked, and the renders show the same arrangement. See the left-group gap.

lamps.note: STS over PWR, the reset pinhole, and the 1/1 port lamp, at the stencil's positions. No document says what any state means.

model.note: TM-280 data sheet (telco.com 2025/12, BATM Networks); the faceplate prints T-Marc 280.

ports.note: 1/1 is a single SFP cage with a lamp to its left (for the port, drawn beside it as in the stencil and the renders); 2/1-2/2 are a ganged pair, common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 turned 180 (lamp windows up, green and amber in the render); 3/1 is a COMBO PORT - "1 x Combo port (10/100/1000Base-T or 100Base-FX / 1000Base-X)" - an SFP cage (port-3-1) beside an RJ45 (copper-3-1, common/rj45-eth@1), one or the other in use at a time. The legend boxes group 1/1 and 3/1 as Network and 2/1-2/2 as Access.

power.note: "5VDC @3A (max) with external power adaptor (AC to DC, DC to DC)", and the faceplate prints 5VDC 3A with a polarity symbol over the barrel inlet: two circles joined through a dot with an arc on its right, as the render shows it. The signs inside the circles are not legible in any render and the stencil draws them differently, so POLARITY IS NOT MODELLED - the circles are drawn plain. No watts are published (5 V at 3 A is 15 W at most).

sources.note: The data sheet (2025-12) and an earlier T-Marc 280 edition (2021), four vendor renders of the same three-quarter view (the sharpest is telco.com 2025/12/TM-280.png, 1632 px), and the legacy NetZoom stencil "Telco Systems" (2022), masters TMC-280-x (CF) and (R). No installation guide is public.
